step1_figure.circuit_type: NMOS Pass-Gate Chain (Series Pass-Transistor Logic with Load Capacitance)
step1_figure.description: Figure 10.16(a) illustrates a series cascade of NMOS pass gates with gates tied to VDD passing an input logic signal to the output, suffering only a single threshold voltage drop (VDD - VTHN). Combined with Figure 10.18 (page 324), the circuit drives a 50 fF load capacitance.

output_high_voltage.description: Maximum output voltage passed through the NMOS pass-gate chain for a high input (VDD)

equation.explanation: An NMOS pass transistor turns off when VGS falls to VTHN, meaning the maximum output voltage it can pass is VDD - VTHN. Even with multiple series pass gates whose gates are at VDD, only one threshold voltage hit occurs.
equation.assumptions: Gates tied to VDD; substrate tied to ground (body effect increases VTHN above nominal Vth0).

sky130_expected.calculation: With VDD = 1.8 V and zero-bias NMOS threshold Vth0 = 0.42 V, body effect with VSB ≈ 1.1 V increases VTHN to approximately 0.65 V - 0.72 V. Therefore, VOH = VDD - VTHN ≈ 1.8 V - 0.70 V = 1.10 V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Without body effect, VOH = 1.8 - 0.42 = 1.38 V. With source-to-substrate body bias, threshold voltage rises, limiting output swing to ~1.05 V - 1.20 V.

output_low_voltage.description: Minimum output voltage passed through the NMOS pass-gate chain for a low input (0 V)

equation.explanation: NMOS pass transistors maintain VGS = VDD when pulling down to ground, remaining strongly on until VDS reaches 0 V. NMOS passes a strong logic '0'.
equation.assumptions: Input driven to 0 V; switch fully enabled with gate at VDD.

sky130_expected.calculation: VOL = 0.0 V, exactly pulled down to ground.
sky130_expected.reasoning: NMOS transistors have negligible offset when conducting to ground in steady-state.

threshold_voltage_drop.description: Voltage drop across the NMOS pass gate chain when passing a logic 1

equation.explanation: Characterizes the threshold degradation when transmitting a high logic level through NMOS pass switches.
equation.assumptions: Source follower action cutoff as VGS approaches VTHN.

sky130_expected.calculation: Vdrop = VDD - VOH = 1.8 V - 1.12 V = 0.68 V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Includes standard zero-bias threshold (0.42 V) plus body effect penalty.

propagation_delay_low_to_high.description: Propagation delay time for output rising to 50% of its swing

equation.explanation: Delay through series pass gates charging load capacitance CL. R_total is the aggregate on-resistance of the 10 series NMOS devices.
equation.assumptions: CL (50 fF) dominates parasitic intermediate capacitances; measured at 50% of input transition to 50% of output swing.

sky130_expected.calculation: For W/L = 1.0u/0.15u, ID,sat ≈ 1.7 mA, Rn ≈ VDD/ID,sat ≈ 1.05 kΩ per transistor. For 10 series devices, R_total ≈ 10.5 kΩ. Then tPLH ≈ 0.7 * 10.5 kΩ * 50 fF ≈ 368 ps. Considering channel resistance increase as VGS decreases toward VOH, effective delay is ~400 ps - 800 ps.
sky130_expected.reasoning: As output rises, VGS decreases from VDD to VTHN, increasing the dynamic on-resistance and slowing the final pull-up.

propagation_delay_high_to_low.description: Propagation delay time for output discharging from VOH to 50% of swing

equation.explanation: Delay discharging load capacitance CL through the 10 series NMOS pass gates to ground.
equation.assumptions: All series NMOS devices are strongly inverted with gate at VDD and source pulling toward 0 V.

sky130_expected.calculation: During pull-down, VGS = 1.8 V is constant for all devices, keeping Rn low (Rn ≈ 1 kΩ per stage, R_total ≈ 10 kΩ). tPHL ≈ 0.7 * 10 kΩ * 50 fF ≈ 350 ps.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Discharging is faster than charging because VGS remains high at VDD throughout the transition.

fall_time.description: Output fall time from 90% to 10% of output swing

equation.explanation: Standard 10%-90% transition time for an RC discharging circuit.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Corresponds to 2.2 * RC with R_total ≈ 10 kΩ and CL = 50 fF.

rise_time.description: Output rise time from 10% to 90% of output swing

equation.explanation: Transition time charging CL through the pass-transistor chain.
equation.assumptions: Measured between 10% and 90% of steady-state VOH.

sky130_expected.calculation: tLH ≈ 2.2 * R_total * CL ≈ 2.2 * 10 kΩ * 50 fF = 1.1 ns, but slowed by NMOS pinch-off near VOH to ~1.4 ns.
sky130_expected.reasoning: As Vout nears VDD - VTHN, device current decreases substantially, elongating the 10%-90% rise time.

step3_testbench.description: Transient simulation of a 10-transistor NMOS pass gate chain driving a 50 fF load capacitance to measure VOH, VOL, threshold voltage drop, propagation delays (tPLH, tPHL), and transition times (rise and fall times).
step3_testbench.spice:
* NMOS Pass-Gate Chain Testbench (SKY130)
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=1.0u L_xm1=0.15u
.param W_xm2=1.0u L_xm2=0.15u
.param W_xm3=1.0u L_xm3=0.15u
.param W_xm4=1.0u L_xm4=0.15u
.param W_xm5=1.0u L_xm5=0.15u
.param W_xm6=1.0u L_xm6=0.15u
.param W_xm7=1.0u L_xm7=0.15u
.param W_xm8=1.0u L_xm8=0.15u
.param W_xm9=1.0u L_xm9=0.15u
.param W_xm10=1.0u L_xm10=0.15u

* Power supply and input signal
VDD VDD 0 DC 1.8
Vin Vin 0 PULSE(0 1.8 1n 50p 50p 6n 14n)

* DUT (NMOS Pass-Gate Chain)
xm1 N001 VDD Vin 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm1} l={L_xm1}
xm2 N002 VDD N001 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm2} l={L_xm2}
xm3 N003 VDD N002 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm3} l={L_xm3}
xm4 N004 VDD N003 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm4} l={L_xm4}
xm5 N005 VDD N004 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm5} l={L_xm5}
xm6 N006 VDD N005 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm6} l={L_xm6}
xm7 N007 VDD N006 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm7} l={L_xm7}
xm8 N008 VDD N007 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm8} l={L_xm8}
xm9 N009 VDD N008 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm9} l={L_xm9}
xm10 Vout VDD N009 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm10} l={L_xm10}
C1 Vout 0 5e-14

.control
tran 10p 16n

* Measure output voltage levels
meas tran voh max v(Vout) from=5n to=7n
meas tran vol min v(Vout) from=13n to=15n
let vdrop = 1.8 - voh
print vdrop

* 50% points for delay measurements
let v_mid_in = 0.9
let v_mid_out = (voh + vol) / 2

meas tran t_delay_lh trig v(Vin) val=0.9 rise=1 targ v(Vout) val=0.55 rise=1
meas tran t_delay_hl trig v(Vin) val=0.9 fall=1 targ v(Vout) val=0.55 fall=1

* 10% to 90% transition levels based on output swing
let v_10 = vol + 0.1 * (voh - vol)
let v_90 = vol + 0.9 * (voh - vol)

meas tran t_rise trig v(Vout) val=0.11 rise=1 targ v(Vout) val=1.00 rise=1
meas tran t_fall trig v(Vout) val=1.00 fall=1 targ v(Vout) val=0.11 fall=1

print voh vol vdrop t_delay_lh t_delay_hl t_rise t_fall
quit
.endc
.end
